chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Saʿd ibn Bakr, from Ḥabīb al-Khathʿamī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: when a man sits for the tashahhud, and he praises Allah and extols Him, that suffices for him.

key_terms.أَثْنَى: he extolled, meaning he spoke words of commendation and glorification
key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: it sufficed him, meaning it fulfilled the minimum required
key_terms.اللَّهَ: Allah, the One being praised in the tashahhud
key_terms.فَحَمِدَ: then he praised, meaning he offered praise to Allah
key_terms.لِلتَّشَهُّدِ: for the tashahhud, the sitting testimony in salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum that suffices in the tashahhud during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the minimum that suffices in the tashahhud during salat (prayer). It shows that praising Allah and extolling Him in that sitting fulfills the required minimum in this context.
